narrative.overview:
Chronicle is designed like a small, carefully made piece of creator hardware on a personal desk: the rail is the instrument chassis, the orange action is the commit key, amber is the live readout, and every fact sits on a readable measurement surface. Pixel structure is functional rather than nostalgic decoration. It helps a single administrator scan cost, status, time, and next action without turning ownership into a game.

The visual world is phosphor-black and gunmetal with bone text, putty rules, safety-orange actions, and a restrained signal palette. Surfaces are flat and exact at rest; depth comes from tonal layering and soft ambient shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Pixel-unit geometry: 8px rhythm, square controls, 2px corners, crisp borders.
Gunmetal chassis surfaces with bone readouts and amber/cyan/lime signal states.
A stable left instrument rail on desktop and compact horizontal controls on mobile.
One clear live readout per surface; no decorative gamification or fake telemetry.
Charts and history remain content-first, with the same palette as navigation and forms.

rules.name: The Signal Economy Rule
rules.body: Orange commits, amber reports, cyan supports, lime confirms, and rose warns. No signal color becomes page decoration.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Large mono numbers are for values people compare; body copy does not become mono just to look technical.

rules.name: The Chassis Rule
rules.body: A surface gets one structural border or one ambient shadow, never a stack of competing chrome.

dos: Do use the 8px rhythm and square 2px corners across routes.
Do reserve orange for actions and active navigation, amber for readouts and focus, and signal colors for explicit state.
Do keep cost, status, activity, and recovery facts visible before decoration.
Do retain strong focus states, 42–44px touch targets, keyboard access, and readable Chinese body copy.
Do let empty, loading, error, and unknown-cost states teach the next action.
donts: Don't turn the asset ledger into a game, score board, or decorative pixel-art toy.
Don't use emoji or arbitrary Unicode glyphs as interface icons; use the existing SVG icon system.
Don't use gradients for text, glassmorphism, pill-shaped card grids, or decorative side-stripe borders.
Don't use mono type for long prose or hide action labels behind icon-only controls on mobile.
Don't make unknown values look like zero or allow color alone to communicate a state.
